products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory, also called Shanghai AI Lab, describes itself as a research institution focused on artificial intelligence, large models, embodied intelligence, safe and trustworthy AI, AI for Science, foundational platforms, and related fields. Its website states that since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten universities, including Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University. The lab presents a 2026 WAIC science frontier forum where it and partners released ten joint innovation achievements in life sciences, materials science, and deep space astronomy.

At that forum, the lab announced a scientific discovery platform called Shusheng Duanyan, which it says connects scientific large models, specialized agents, experimental data, and embodied automation equipment across the full research process from hypothesis to experimental verification. It also describes a Shusheng embodied full-stack engine called Intern-Robotics for data, training, and real-world application in embodied intelligence. The lab's stated safety approach includes an AI-45-degree balance law, under which AI safety and performance should develop along a 45-degree angle, with short-term fluctuation allowed but not long-term deviation below or above that line, and a causal path through general alignment, intervenability, and reflection.

The lab is classified as a non-profit government laboratory. Its product InternLM is a Chinese open-source large language model with an academic research focus, and cross-border data review is advised.
